articles.title: Inside the 'Lion’s Den': Real estate brothers bragged about 'hunting' women before 30-year prison terms
articles.summary: New Peacock docuseries "The Wolves of Real Estate" reveals texts where Oren Alexander wrote of "hunting" women before his 30-year sex trafficking sentence.
articles.body: The Alexander brothers sold multimillion-dollar mansions, mingled with the wealthy and lived like real estate golden boys. But behind the luxury and excess, prosecutors said, was a decades-long pattern of sexual abuse. In text messages presented at trial and featured in a new docuseries, the brothers and their associates discussed "hunting" for women. "We are running out of prey," Oren wrote in one message. Convicted of federal sex trafficking offenses and each sentenced to 30 years in prison, Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander are the subjects of a new Peacock true crime docuseries, "The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers," which features accounts from women who say the trio sexually assaulted them. ALEXANDER BROTHERS ALLEGEDLY PAID FOR COVERAGE OF SEX-TRAFFICKING TRIAL AS WRITERS DENY FAVORABLE TREATMENT "The brothers at trial, they said, 'We're not predators, we were just playboys,’" director Emma Schwartz told Fox News Digital. "But at the same time, you see their own words. Oren says he would hunt women like he hunts a client. And that's not exactly language about seducing people. The word 'hunt' was used a lot in their messages." "The prosecutor's theory to the jury, and the public, was that these men invited women out to the Hamptons, women who traveled through New York, and the whole purpose was to sexually assault or rape them," Schwartz said. "There were messages like, 'Let's orgy them out,' with a clear intent that sex was involved." The Alexander brothers, born into wealth, grew up to be real estate golden boys. Oren and Tal, former star brokers at Douglas Elliman, later co-founded their own real estate firm specializing in luxury properties in Miami, New York City and Los Angeles. The brothers were involved in high-profile real estate transactions, including a nearly $240 million penthouse sale in 2019 that set a record for the most expensive residential sale in U.S. history. They co-founded the luxury real estate firm Official in 2022. Alon was an executive at his family's private security company. Together, they moved in elite circles and hosted lavish parties in Miami, New York City, the Hamptons and Aspen. Court filings previously obtained by Fox News Digital alleged that the brothers used "the promise of luxury experiences, travel and accommodations" to lure women to locations where they were then sexually assaulted. According to the docuseries, the brothers exchanged messages in secret group chats, including one message that read, "Welcome to the Lion's Den." The conversations included discussions about "hunting" for women and what the participants expected in return. "All content in this chat stays in the chat," one text shown in the film warned. In another text shown in the film, Oren said "boys need to hunt" because "we are running out of prey." He appeared to write, "Met a cute Canadian and took her back to the crib and trained her." When one person texted, "No is not an option," Oren replied, "Nope." In a separate group chat, Oren warned that the "boys are hungry," while Tal wrote, "Girls look fresh," according to court documents. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Prosecutors later alleged in a court filing that the brothers raped or sexually assaulted at least 70 women, describing them as "serial rapists." Several women described receiving gifts and being flown to luxury destinations where they said they were given drugs before being assaulted. "The only thing can bring us down is some h-- complaining," one text attributed to Oren read in the film. "I think the most surprising thing was some of the messages that came out, things that they put in writing themselves as the way they and their friends talked about women," Schwartz said. "Often, it was very uncomfortable and hard to hear. They used language like they want to get 'the best ROI' on bringing women on a trip, as if women are property or something to get a return on investment. There's also a blog post where their friends had outlined a certain psychology about why they get pleasure out of hurting women. Those messages got into a sense of how they thought about things." "People can say that they've never done that," Schwartz said. "But when you see over and over things in writing that speak to not believing in consent, it's a lot easier to believe when a woman gets up there and testifies about what happened." Prosecutors said the brothers' alleged sexual abuse dated back more than two decades, to their high school years in Miami. For the docuseries, Schwartz interviewed several former students who attended the same high school as the brothers or knew them personally. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS "There was more than one person who said, 'I'm not entirely surprised by the allegations that came out,'" Schwartz said. "They had felt there had been similar, or in the beginning, patterns that one might see later on." "These cases can be really difficult, especially when you have teenagers who may not always tell their own story straight because they don't want to admit what they did or that they snuck out and something happened," she said. "I think there's always questions about what lessons someone could have learned, and those were questions that some of the people who went to high school with them still had." "There were allegations that went back a very long time," Schwartz added. The brothers' downfall began in June 2024, when two civil lawsuits accusing Oren and Alon of sexual assault became public. As more women came forward with similar allegations, the FBI investigated accusations of sexual violence spanning more than a decade. On Dec. 11, 2024, all three brothers were arrested in Miami on federal sex trafficking charges. Prosecutors accused the trio of using their wealth and status to lure women to lavish parties, luxury properties and exclusive trips, where prosecutors said the women were drugged and sexually assaulted. SIGN UP TO GET THE TRUE CRIME NEWSLETTER During their six-week trial, 11 women testified against the brothers, including several who said they were minors at the time of the encounters. Lindsey Acree, an artist and gallery owner, testified that she was raped by Tal and another man at a Hamptons home in 2011 after taking a drink that she said left her feeling paralyzed. "The biggest thing is why? Why did you do this?" Acree asked. "I don’t understand the cruelty. I don’t understand the hatred toward women." Another woman who said Tal raped her in August 2014 told the court she carried "a quiet funeral in me for the person I might have become had this not happened to me." LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Every second that Tal raped me in that shower felt like an eternity of terror," the woman, who used a pseudonym, said. Another woman, describing her rape at a Hamptons mansion, said, "What looked like a beautiful place became for me a mansion of horror, a mansion of dark secrets." Lexi Zettle said Tal was once "a prince in my eyes" who offered her the promise of a "fairytale" romance before he began pressuring her to have sex with his business associates. GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB "They treated me like a rag doll, like I was this disposable thing," Zettle said. On March 9, 2026, a federal jury in New York City found the brothers guilty. All three were convicted of multiple federal sex offenses, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking. On Oct. 27, they were each sentenced to 30 years in prison. U.S. District Judge Valerie E. Caproni told them, "Your conduct was monstrous," equating them to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. SEND US A TIP The brothers argued that becoming husbands and fathers had changed them from their womanizing ways. While none of them testified at trial, each spoke before their sentencing. Oren said he and his brothers came of age at the height of hookup culture and regretted many of the things he said about women. Still, he insisted they had never broken the law. A tearful Tal said, "I feel like an atomic bomb has been dropped on my life and destroyed everything in its wake." Alon said he had built a different life since his partying years. "Thirty years is a very long sentence," Schwartz said. "They'll be almost 70. Each of them has children and will essentially miss their entire childhood." Schwartz hopes the docuseries will challenge common misconceptions about sex trafficking and shed light on how victims can be exploited. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE In response to the documentary producers' questions, Tal denied pressuring Zettle to have sex with potential clients. Oren denied sexually assaulting Acree and said she continued to socialize with him. All three brothers denied drugging or sexually assaulting anyone and said they planned to appeal their convictions. articles.title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Communist, hard-left groups mount global youth strike to bring 'socialist revolution'
articles.summary: An analysis finds 114 communist, Marxist and socialist groups powered the "International Youth Strike" across 24 countries, with red flags in the streets.
articles.body: Red hammer-and-sickle flags flew over Europe at protests across the continent Friday, but media coverage barely mentioned them. Media outlets described the day's demonstrations as "youth protests" over wages, schools, climate, "austerity" and the alleged "genocide" in Israel. The streets told a different story. A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that a transnational network of self-described communist, Marxist and socialist groups organized the protests with an explicitly ideological appeal: using party banners, mass-produced recruitment posters and calls for a "communist mass movement" and "socialist revolution." Officials in Hamburg, Germany, warned that "left-wing extremist" groups were behind the Friday actions. In Milan, a young woman wore a red hammer-and-sickle shirt, raising her fist among demonstrators holding placards that read "FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE" above small branding for "Youth International Strike Against War," the socialist coalition that organized the day's actions. By late Friday, the protests were promoted by BreakThrough News, a nonprofit funded by Neville Roy Singham, an American-born communist tech tycoon living in Shanghai , supporting the Chinese Communist Party and President Xi Jinping's "new world order." According to a Fox News Digital analysis, the "International Youth Strike" brought together 114 communist youth organizations, revolutionary Marxist and socialist groups alongside far-left student unions, climate campaigners and anti-Israel activists. The official website lists actions in 24 countries. A Fox News Digital tracker of groups involved in the International Youth Strike finds that most of them self-describe as communist, Marxist, Trotskyist, socialist or far-left. The remaining entries include education, environmental and other issue-based organizations, as well as groups whose ideology hasn't been established. CHAOS INC.: WHO'S WHO IN THE GLOBAL MAYHEM NETWORK? COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE FROM 'RED SPROUTS' TO SCHOOL BOARD RACES, DSA'S YEARS-LONG EFFORT TO REACH CHILDREN GAINS MOMENTUM The mobilization in Europe comes after Democratic Socialists of America celebrated its midterm election victories by declaring that voters had "emphatically endorsed socialism." In the U.K., members of Socialist Students, one of the lead organizers, marched behind bright red banners that read, "FIGHT FOR A SOCIALIST FUTURE." Also in the U.K., the Revolutionary Communist Students urged members to walk out of school under the slogan "SMASH IMPERIALISM / FIGHT FOR REVOLUTION." A wing of Revolutionary Communist International, a global organization that runs Marxist.com, the group promoted the protest with a video of members holding copies of their newspaper, the "Communist." And their members turned out in Cambridge, Liverpool, Leeds, Newcastle and Brighton in the U.K. The platform framed the protests as "YOUTH-LED STRIKES ACROSS EUROPE AGAINST WAR AND LIVING COSTS." It featured a representative of Sindicat d’Estudiants in Spain without identifying the group's revolutionary Marxist politics as "revolutionary communists" with Barcelona headquarters at Casal Marxista, or "Marxist House." The protests played into anti-West narratives, and Press TV, Iran's official propaganda network, published a story about youth protests "over wages and living costs." The mobilization follows student blockades and nationwide demonstrations in France, where Fox News Digital established that a network of far-left groups, including communists, socialists and Antifa, helped orchestrate the unrest. The strike's manifesto seeks NATO’s "dissolution" and "radical system change," placing students alongside the working class as a "revolutionary force." In Rome, one sign featured the silhouette of Marxist guerrilla Che Guevara and demanded, "CHE IS DEAD / STEP UP." BEHIND FRANCE'S STUDENT RIOTS: COMMUNISTS, UNIONS AND A GLOBAL PROPAGANDA NETWORK In Hamburg, the Ministry of the Interior and Sport's State Office for the Protection of the Constitution published a report on on Wednesday warning about "linksextremistische," or "left-wing extremist" groups playing a "significant role" in coordinating the protests. Hamburg government officials said protest organizers weren't concerned about legitimate debate over policy issues, like the economy or conscription, but warned about "enemies of the constitution who attempt to exploit these and other legitimate causes for their anti-democratic ideology, for example, through relevant images and videos on social media." For example, Young Struggle, a Europe-wide socialist group, founded in Stuttgart, Germany, said that its members are "struggling against a system of capitalism, of endless exploitation, of war, imperialism and patriarchy." In another report, Hamburg officials warned that Young Struggle is a wing of a Turkish left-wing extremist group, the Marxist-Leninist Communist Party. Young Struggle blasted its triumphs from the protests on social media, with menacing fast-cut videos, as Hamburg officials warned they would do from Lyon, France, Austria and elsewhere, and the message: "LA JEUNESSE PRÉPARE LA RÉVOLUTION (THE YOUTH PREPARES THE REVOLUTION." "What we're witnessing in Europe is part of a pattern of malign actors using students and youth as foot-soldiers in protest movements," Brandy Shufutinsky, director of education and national security at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank based in Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital. "In the U.S. we've seen these entities attempt to connect things like climate justice, immigration, and workers' rights to boycotts and sanctions against Israel," said Shufutinsky, a trained social worker. "Often, these organizations form 'youth' wings as a way to garner support for their movements amongst younger generations. This happened with the formation of the Soviet Union, Nazi Germany, Communist China and Islamist Iran." Many of the European strike organizers explicitly call for revolutionary changes to governance, ownership, wealth, taxes, laws and political power, much like in the U.S. Germany’s Socialist German Workers’ Youth, another protest organizer, says it grounds its mission in "Marx, Engels and Lenin." Its theory page invokes Vladimir Lenin’s declaration: "Without revolutionary theory there can be no revolutionary movement." Fellow signatory REVOLUTION, operating in Germany, Austria and elsewhere, describes itself as an "independent communist youth organization." Its mission advocates "revolutionary overthrow," a "communist mass movement" and a "world party of socialist revolution." Sweden’s Revolutionary Communist Youth, which led protests, identifies its ideological foundation as "Marxism-Leninism" and describes organizing through "class struggle." Symbols of the far-left Antifa movement, which the Trump administration declared a terrorist group, also appeared at protests. In Tel Aviv, Israel, the far-left emerged with an "ANTIFA ACTION" flag, much like one that fluttered in Cologne, Germany, where protesters flew a flag with the message, "ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION," meaning "Anti-Fascist Action" in German, commonly associated with Antifa. The name originated with a campaign launched by Germany’s Communist Party in 1932. Today, its familiar two-flag emblem is used by antifascist groups and activists worldwide. Italy In Italy, demonstrators marched beneath communist party flags, hammer-and-sickle emblems and historical resistance banners. In Turin in northwestern Italy, near the French border, members of the Confederazione Generale Italiana del Lavoro, or the Italian General Confederation of Labour, filled a square, waving red hammer-and-sickle flags and protesting beside members of the Partito Comunista dei Lavoratori, or Workers' Communist Party, a far-left, Trotskyist political party. Italy’s Giovani Comunisti, the Communist Refoundation Party's youth organization, joined the protests, too. The group describes its members as "proudly communist." Its website promotes Marxist political education under the instruction: "Educate yourselves. Agitate. Organize." Others marched behind a banner marked "FC-FGC," referring to the Communist Front (Fronte Comunista, FC) and the Front of Communist Youth (Fronte della Gioventù Comunista, FGC). In Rome, a flag with the hammer and sickle and the name "Partito Comunista Rivoluzionario," Italian for "Revolutionary Communist Party," flew at a protest, along with a flag of Cuba, a symbol of support for the Communist Party of Cuba. Nearby, members of the Garibaldi Brigades, named after a formation of the Italian Communist Party that fought in the resistance during World War II, waved their flag with a red star over the Italian tricolor. A demonstrator also carried a flag of the former Soviet Union over his shoulder, while a red hammer-and-sickle flag appeared beside Palestinian flags at the monument to Giuseppe Garibaldi, a 19th century revolutionary who led guerrilla fighters called "Redshirts." Activists of a Marxist–Leninist party, Fronte Comunista (Communist Front), unfurled their hammer-and-sickle flag on the streets. In Milan, a protester dressed as Karl Marx, the communist theorist, carried a depiction of his treatise, "Das Kapital." United States The mobilization also drew support from American communist and socialist organizations. In Los Angeles, the Party for Socialism and Liberation held a Friday evening forum to discuss global student protests. The communist group works closely with the nonprofit network funded by Singham. In Denver, Denver Communists, Colorado Revolutionary Communists and other far-leftists descended on the Colorado State Capitol with demands expressed by the "youth strike" movement: the "abolition of all forms of military conscription," solidarity with the "struggles of oppressed peoples around the world, starting with the Palestinian people," "climate justice and social justice," "radical transformation of the system we live in" and a challenge to "authoritarianism, repression and the far right." United Kingdom In Britain, political organizations used recruitment placards, newspapers and advertisements to reach potential supporters with Marxism 101. At King's College London, a protester carried a copy of the "Socialist Worker" newspaper alongside fliers promoting "MARXISM IN A DAY!" – a Nov. 28 event sponsored by the Socialist Workers Party. "Revolts have broken out across the world. From Paris, to Mumbai, from Madrid to Milan, from Tirana to Lisbon - the youth is taking to the streets to fight for a better world," the event promotion says. "Now more than ever, revolutionary Marxist ideas are crucial to the fight backs against a world of capitalist catastrophe," it continues. The promotion promises "socialists and anti-fascist campaigners from France," including Zoé Lewkowicz, a French socialist and "anti-fascist" organizer with Autonomie de Classe, a revolutionary socialist organization based in Paris. In London, a man held a red flare in front of signs that declared "FIGHT FOR SOCIALISM," while demonstrators covered their faces with keffiyehs and surgical masks beside red hammer-and-sickle flags and Socialist Worker placards declaring, "FOLLOW FRANCE: FIGHT THE SYSTEM." Like professional protest organizers do in the U.S., Socialist Worker activists piled pre-made signs at a lamppost for demonstrators to pick up just before the 9 a.m. The placards were bundled with tape around their wooden handles and grouped by message. An image of a Malcolm X appeared on one design bearing the demand: "FIGHT FOR SOCIALISM!" Others said: "JOIN SOCIALIST STUDENTS." Soon, the recruitment message was moving through the crowd. Surrounded by police in reflective vests, marchers carried the signs piled moments earlier against the lamppost. Germany In Bremen, Germany, marchers carried a flag marked "ANTIFA" behind a banner depicting a clenched fist holding a pencil in front of a globe with the message "NOT THEIR WARS." They marched in front of a flag that said, "JUGEND GEGEN WEHRPFLICHT, AFSK LEIBNIZPLATZ." "AFSK" refers to the Antifaschistisches Schüler:innen Kollektiv, an "antifascist" collective in Bremen that mobilizes students to join "red blocs," or "roter block." "Jugend gegen wehrpflicht" means "Youth against conscription." Researchers at Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, a center-right think tank, have also warned that far-left groups use these student demonstrations to channel youth frustration toward broader far-left, pro-Russian foreign policy narratives. In Bochum, a man with a white beard and mustache carried a sign bearing the initials "DKP" for the German Communist Party. His poster read, "Stoppt die Kriegsvorbereitungen," or "Stop the preparations for war." It also bore the message, "Nein zur Wehrpflicht," or "No to conscription." It continued: "Bundeswehr raus aus Schulen und Universitäten" — "German armed forces out of schools and universities." In Bochum, students carried a banner, "GenZ Regelt," as "GenZ sorts it," beside another banner, "Sozialismus regelt," translated as, "Socialism will sort it out" or "Socialism fixes it," with generational branding while downplaying explicit socialist messaging. West Bank and Gaza From London to Berlin, the Palestinian flag and keffiyeh scarf, representing Palestinian "resistance" to a Jewish state of Israel, was a fixture at protests, even flapping outside the Colosseum in Rome beside the tricolor flag of the Garibaldi Brigades. In the West Bank and Gaza, 11 Palestinian groups associated with the Boycott, Divest and Sanctions Movement, whose officials have said they seek the end of a Jewish state of Israel, issued an announcement supporting the youth actions and called for the "right of our refugees to return to their homes and receive reparations." 'International Socialist Youth Network' The mobilization's planning meetings show ambitions extending beyond Friday. According to Britain’s Socialist Party, 12 organizations from eight countries met in Cologne on June 14, months before France’s autumn unrest. Socialist Students proposed the campaign’s slogan, "Fight for Our Futures, Not Their Wars." Its own mission seeks a "socialist transformation of society." By the time of an Oct. 17 meeting in Paris, participation had grown to 27 organizations from 11 countries. Delegates discussed connecting national grievances under the international banner, joined the street demonstration and agreed to continue organizing after Nov. 20, according to Socialist Students’ account. A larger conference is planned in Italy in February 2027. Socialist Students urged that gathering to establish an "international socialist youth network," making the walkouts a potential recruiting ground for a continuing political action. In the United Kingdom, Shabbir Lakha, a national spokesman for the "Stop the War Coalition," stood on a stage at Downing Street, accusing governments of having "facilitated the genocide in Gaza" and urging demonstrators to unite to "break their imperialist power." The coalition doesn't list its donors. At day's end, Stop the War Coalition shared a Guardian article, headlined "Young people across Europe stage coordinated 'fight for our future' protests." There was no mention of the communist and socialist ideological underpinnings of the protests or the hammer-and-sickle flags and revolutionary banners that defined the day on the streets. The coalition also promoted another mobilization for Jan. 23, calling for yet another "mass movement against war, militarism and austerity" – and socialism and communism. articles.title: MEA clears Taj Mahal visit for Pakistan delegation, no nod for Nizamuddin dargah

articles.body: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday clarified that permission has been granted for the Pakistani delegation to visit the Taj Mahal, while its proposed visit to Nizamuddin dargah in Delhi has not received security clearance.According to news agency ANI, the delegation, led by Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination Musadik Masood Malik, was also cleared to visit Humayun's Tomb and Dilli Haat in Delhi. The delegation is in India to attend the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum from November 20 to 22.Malik had expressed his desire to visit several historical landmarks in India, including the Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb, during his stay in the country. The Pakistani minister said he wanted to explore India, meet its people and understand its culture.The Centre had earlier clarified that no general travel restrictions had been imposed on visiting Pakistani ministers and that they were free to travel anywhere in India, including the Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb.The Pakistani delegation arrived at Purana Qila in New Delhi on Friday to participate in the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.Malik's visit marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years. He was received at the airport by Pakistan High Commission's Chargé d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich.Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum on Friday evening. The three-day programme focuses on the shared and interconnected civilisational heritage of SCO countries, cross-cultural engagement and people-to-people ties.The initiative follows a proposal made by PM Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025, to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the grouping. The forum features thematic sessions on cultural expressions, art and architecture, language and literary traditions, and monastic and philosophical heritage.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Failed to redraw world': Zelenskyy mocks Russia over China summit, says event 'unsuccessful' for Putin
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday described this week's trilateral summit involving the United States, Russia and China as \"very
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday described this week's trilateral summit involving the United States, Russia and China as "very unsuccessful" for Russian President Vladimir Putin. He said that the Russian leader had failed in his attempt to recreate the 1945 Yalta conference that shaped Europe's post-war order.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine's prospects of joining NATO after the war remained uncertain, despite the issue being discussed at this week's Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin. He said Kyiv was still unclear whether it would be able to join the military alliance, a long-standing goal for Ukraine.The remarks came amid escalating Russian attacks on Ukraine and growing tensions across Europe. Zelenskyy also accused Putin of having no intention of ending the war and said Russia was seeking to intensify the conflict.Zelenskyy criticises Putin after China summitZelenskyy's comments followed a meeting between US President Donald Trump, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Thursday.The Ukrainian leader said Putin had failed to achieve his objective through the summit. He referred to the Yalta conference of 1945, where the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and Britain discussed the post-war settlement of Europe.Separately, Zelenskyy criticised Trump's description of Putin as his "friend". In an interview with CNN on Friday, he called the Russian president "a killer"."For us, he is an enemy. And of course, for us, he is a killer," Zelenskyy said. He warned that describing the Russian leader in friendly terms could mean "he doesn’t feel enough pressure."Russia launches one of its biggest attacks on UkraineMeanwhile, Russia launched more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, at Ukraine overnight on Friday, Zelenskyy said."Putin launched this attack in a highly demonstrative manner – following weak meetings in China and the actual failure of his attempt to somehow 'redraw' the world," Zelenskyy said on Telegram.He said Russia also used missiles carrying cluster warheads. Zelenskyy described the tactics as "especially vile", alleging that Russian forces fired missiles in groups with pauses of 20 to 30 minutes between strikes.The intervals were intended to make it harder for emergency teams to extinguish fires, clear rubble and restore essential services, he said.Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown kills twoA Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine, killed two people and wounded 60 others on Friday night, local officials said on Saturday.The victims were a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city administration, said on Telegram. Regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha said six children were among the injured.The attack triggered four fires and damaged around 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and vehicles, Vilkul said.He alleged that Russian forces launched further strikes after emergency teams reached the site.“First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers, and utility workers,” Vilkul wrote.Elsewhere, 11 people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone struck a five-storey apartment building in the Kharkiv region. Another person was wounded in an attack on Kyiv, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said.Zelenskyy defends attacks on Crimean BridgeZelenskyy on Saturday defended Ukraine's repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge, which connects occupied Crimea with mainland Russia, calling them a "fair response" to Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges.Speaking during a meeting with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv, Zelenskyy said Russia had attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.“Putin attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.”“Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said. “This is important, that’s why it’s our absolutely fair response.”He also rejected Putin's claim that the bridge was used exclusively for civilian traffic.“If he can use internet, he can use it and see tanks, armored vehicles, artillery,” the Ukrainian leader said.Streeting described the violations of Polish airspace as “an outrageous provocation” and called on Ukraine's allies to increase their support.“The more they try and deter Europe from supporting Ukraine, the more we will step up,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Arman Shpuza, the Georgia student who designed a tiny turbine that generates electricity from rainwater flowing through drainpipes and won a national invention award in 2026
articles.summary: Arman Shpuza, a ninth-grade student from Georgia, has won two awards at the Raytheon Technologies Invention Convention US Nationals with Ampipe, a tiny
articles.body: Arman Shpuza, a ninth-grade student from Georgia, has won two awards at the Raytheon Technologies Invention Convention US Nationals with Ampipe, a tiny turbine system installed in downspouts that converts the energy of falling rain into electricity. According to the K-12 InVenture Prize, he took the Innovation Process: Best Logbook Award and Second Place for Ninth Grade on 5 June 2026 in Dearborn, Michigan. He competed as an independent student for the first time. The idea began when he watched rain fall outside his window during a heavy storm, and he is now working on further improvements with a patent in mind.How Arman Shpuza developed Ampipe, a rainwater-powered turbine systemShpuza is the inventor of Ampipe, and the invention is a tiny turbine system installed in downspouts that converts the energy of falling rain into electricity. The programme's report of 9 June 2026 describes it as "a tiny turbine system installed in downspouts that converts the energy of falling rain into electricity."The idea came from a heavy storm. In the K-12 InVenture Prize's report of 15 July 2026, Trammell writes that Shpuza got the idea from watching rain fall outside his window during a heavy storm. Something about the rain reminded him of a hydroelectric plant, "and an idea for an invention was born, just like that." The report says Ampipe's artificial intelligence system was inspired by his uncle in Sweden.Arman Shpuza earns national recognition for his Ampipe inventionThe Raytheon Technologies Invention Convention US Nationals Award Ceremony took place on 5 June at The Henry Ford in Dearborn, Michigan. The 9 June 2026 report states that Shpuza "won a Best Logbook Award as well as Second Place for Ninth Grade." The 15 July 2026 report gives the fuller title of the first award as the Innovation Process: Best Logbook Award. It also says he earned the Constellations Energy Award and a patent application award at State Finals at Georgia Tech in March.Danyelle Larkin, director of the K-12 InVenture Prize programme, is quoted in the 9 June report as saying: "We are so proud of all of our students who represented our state at U.S. Nationals." She added: "Team Ampipe was an independent student competing for the first time in the competition, and he earned an application for a patent to take the invention to the marketplace. You really can't do much better than that. What an amazing accomplishment this is from such a self-driven young student."Arman Shpuza explains how repeated testing strengthened his Ampipe projectStudents at Nationals had the chance to engage with representatives from the United States Patent and Trademark Office. They also had the opportunity to pitch their inventions to Shark Tank casting agents and to take part in a youth panel discussion. K-12 InVenture Prize is an affiliate of Invention Convention Worldwide and "reserves several spots to invite select student teams from State Finals to represent Georgia at the U.S. Nationals competition each year."Shpuza said State Finals helped him prepare. In the 15 July 2026 report, he says: "State Finals was really valuable to help me get ready for Nationals. I think the judges' feedback was very useful to see my project from a different perspective, which I think helped me stand out at Nationals." He continues: "I kept going through prototype after prototype, testing and improving my design using the feedback. So, when I got to Nationals, I knew what to expect and felt more confident with my improved project."How family support and persistence helped Arman Shpuza develop AmpipeIn the 15 July 2026 report, Shpuza describes how he felt when his name was called: "It was unforgettable. I wasn't expecting to win at that high level, so when they called my name, I sprang out of my seat. It felt like everything around me paused for a moment." According to the report, he credits his teachers and family, near and far, for supporting his invention journey. These include the Economics for Entrepreneurs and science teachers who sparked his creativity and curiosity, his uncle in Sweden, and his mother, who encouraged him to enter the K-12 InVenture Prize competition with Ampipe.He says: "Ampipe failed several times, and I went through many different iterations, so I think it's really important to persevere and try on, even when things don't go your way." With a patent in mind, he told the K-12 InVenture Prize that he is working on further improvements. In his words: "There is no perfect invention. There is always something you can improve. So, I'm still trying to test different models to see how I can advance Ampipe's efficiency and impact." His advice to other young inventors is to "stay curious about the world around you and find something that you have a personal connection to."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1926, a London home opened for retired theatre workers; 100 years later, producer Cameron Mackintosh has given £2 million for a new assisted-living building honouring Richard and Sheila Attenborough
articles.summary: Theatre producer Sir Cameron Mackintosh has donated £2 million to a London retirement home for performing arts workers, funding a new assisted-living
articles.body: Theatre producer Sir Cameron Mackintosh has donated £2 million to a London retirement home for performing arts workers, funding a new assisted-living building named after the late Lord Richard Attenborough and Lady Sheila Attenborough. The grant comes through the Mackintosh Foundation and goes toward Denville Hall's £26 million Centenary Appeal, according to an announcement published on Cameron Mackintosh's official website and reported by WhatsOnStage on 18 November 2026. Located in Northwood, north-west London, Denville Hall provides care and community for people who have spent their careers on stage, in film, television, and behind the scenes."Denville Hall does extraordinary work for people who have given their lives to the performing arts. Many friends and colleagues have found care and companionship there, in a place where they can remain part of the world they know," Sir Cameron Mackintosh said in a statement reported by Theatre Weekly. The new assisted-living facility will carry the official title of The Richard and Sheila Attenborough Building Funded by the Mackintosh Foundation, according to WhatsOnStage. BroadwayWorld reported that the gift serves as a tribute to Mackintosh's friend Richard Attenborough and to the community Denville Hall has built for generations of stage and screen workers.A lasting link to Richard and Sheila AttenboroughBoth Richard Attenborough and his wife, actress Sheila Sim, had deep ties to the Northwood home long before spending their final years there. According to Denville Hall's historical records and the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, Lord Attenborough served as president of the home, while Lady Attenborough worked as a trustee and vice-president and played a major role in redevelopments during the 1960s and 2000s. The couple had starred together in the original 1952 London cast of Agatha Christie's play The Mousetrap.In June 2012, shortly before her 90th birthday, Lady Attenborough moved into Denville Hall after being diagnosed with dementia. Lord Attenborough joined her there in March 2013 as his own health declined, remaining by her side until his death in August 2014, while Lady Attenborough died in January 2016. "We're grateful to Sir Cameron and the Mackintosh Foundation for helping us build a stronger future for Denville Hall and the people who call it home," Denville Hall said in a statement posted on its social media channels and cited by BroadwayWorld.What the £26 million appeal will fundDenville Hall launched its £26 million Centenary Appeal in spring 2026 to prepare the charity for its second century of service, according to WhatsOnStage. The total fundraising target is split into two equal parts: £13 million for capital building projects across the Northwood site, and £13 million for Alfred's Fund, a new endowment named after founder Alfred Denville to cover future operating costs. As detailed by The Stage and WhatsOnStage, the capital plans include three new buildings featuring independent assisted-living flats alongside a cinema, gym, rehabilitation and yoga studio, restaurant, cafe, and wheelchair-accessible gardens, sitting beside the charity's existing residential, nursing, dementia, and respite care wings.Actors Dame Helen Mirren, Sir Ian McKellen, and Daniel Radcliffe serve as presidents of the Centenary Appeal, while theatre producers Nica Burns and Rosemary Squire lead the wider industry campaign, according to WhatsOnStage. Earlier in 2026, West End shows including Oliver!, The Phantom of the Opera, and Cabaret took part in a "Theatre Gives Day" bucket collection on 18 July, followed by a gala concert at London's Victoria Palace Theatre on 1 November.From a 16th-century farmhouse to a haven for actorsDenville Hall's origins date back to 1924, when actor-manager and member of parliament Alfred Denville bought the Victorian Gothic mansion in Northwood, according to the charity's official history. Built on the site of a 16th-century property known as Maze Farm, the house was dedicated by Denville to the acting profession in memory of his son Jack, who died at age 26 from complications linked to First World War injuries. Princess Louise, the Princess Royal, formally opened Denville Hall on 19 July 1926 as a rest home for retired actors and actresses, and over the past century its doors have opened to all entertainment workers over the age of 70 and their spouses, including dancers, agents, stage crew, and circus performers.Over the decades, major figures from British stage and screen have helped keep the home running. In the late 1960s and early 1970s, stars such as Sean Connery, Michael Caine, Paul Scofield, and Elizabeth Taylor donated performance fees toward rebuilding work. Playwright Terence Rattigan left royalties from his plays to the charity, and in 1999 the original stage set from The Mousetrap was auctioned off after 47 years to raise funds.You use AI every day. articles.title: A US judge blocks Trump's attempt to redirect $1.3 billion from permanent housing into temporary shelters, ruling the changes to a $4 billion homelessness programme unlawful and ordering new grant applications
articles.summary: A US federal judge has ruled against the Trump administration's plan to redirect $1.3 billion in homelessness funding, preserving the integrity of the Continuum of Care program and allowing organizations to resubmit grant applications.
articles.body: A US federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's attempt to redirect $1.3 billion in federal homelessness funding from permanent housing towards temporary accommodation and support services, ruling that the changes to a more than $4 billion programme exceeded the government's authority.US District Judge Mary McElroy ruled on Friday that the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) could not introduce new grant conditions that effectively bypassed requirements established by Congress. She also ordered the agency to reopen the application process, allowing organisations to revise and resubmit their funding requests by December 1.The decision concerns the federal government's Continuum of Care programme, which provides grants to states, local governments and non-profit organisations supporting people experiencing homelessness. Congress appropriated more than $4 billion for the programme in fiscal year 2026, with HUD proposing to reserve $1.3 billion for transitional housing and grants focused solely on supportive services.Why the judge blocked Trump's homelessness funding planThe Continuum of Care programme, established in 1987, has traditionally followed a housing-first model. It prioritises placing people in permanent accommodation without requiring them to meet conditions such as sobriety or employment before receiving housing assistance.The programme also funds services such as childcare, job training, mental health counselling and transportation. Its support is directed towards several vulnerable groups, including veterans, families and people with disabilities.The Trump administration has sought to change these funding priorities, arguing against continuing the existing approach. However, McElroy found that HUD's proposed criteria conflicted with the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, which sets out the framework for distributing the grants.According to the judge, the department's plan could allow it to avoid mandatory assessments of existing projects, including their performance and ability to move people into permanent housing."Although Congress delegated to the secretary the power to create additional criteria for awarding funds, this residual clause cannot be read as allowing HUD to nullify the other congressionally established mandatory factors," McElroy wrote as cited by Reuters.The ruling follows an extended legal dispute over the administration's efforts to overhaul the programme. McElroy had blocked similar changes in 2025 and again earlier this year, but a federal appeals court subsequently lifted the earlier order.Following that decision, 22 mostly Democratic-led states, the District of Columbia and a coalition of housing and homelessness advocacy groups renewed their challenge on different legal grounds. The National Alliance to End Homelessness was among the organisations involved.HUD ordered to reopen grant applications as Turner considers appealMcElroy also struck down other parts of HUD's proposed changes. These included restrictions on grant recipients engaging in activities targeting drug users, such as needle exchange programmes, and a provision that allowed the agency to disqualify applicants that did not adequately promote "self-sufficiency".Under the latest order, HUD must allow applicants to amend and resubmit their grant applications through December 1. The agency has been directed to make the funding awards by December 31.The coalition that challenged the administration's plan welcomed the ruling in a joint statement, saying it "protects the ability of communities and service providers to compete fairly for essential funding without being penalized for providing permanent housing."HUD Secretary Scott Turner said the department reserved the right to appeal the decision. He argued that the ruling had disrupted the funding process just days before the agency was due to announce its awards."This ruling disrupts $4 billion for our most vulnerable, just days before funding awards were set to be made," Turner said.Turner also defended the administration's decision to change the programme's funding priorities, saying HUD would no longer continue what it considered an ineffective approach to homelessness."Under President Trump, HUD is no longer in the business of throwing taxpayers’ money at a status quo that has repeatedly failed America’s most vulnerable," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nearly 400 people helped carve Mount Rushmore; workers climbed 700 stairs and dangled over the mountain as dynamite removed most of the rock
articles.summary: Discover the extraordinary effort behind Mount Rushmore, where nearly 400 workers transformed a granite mountain into a national monument using dynamite and manual labor, climbing 700 stairs daily.
articles.body: For 14 years, hundreds of workers helped transform a granite mountain in South Dakota into one of America’s most notable monuments. This required more than just sculpting skills, as workers climbed 700 stairs to reach their positions, operated heavy machinery and, in some cases, worked while being suspended above the mountain face in small seats which were attached to steel cables. Though dynamite removed most of the rock, drillers and carvers had to shape the remaining granite by hand.According to the National Park Service (NPS), nearly 400 men and women contributed to the Mount Rushmore project. These workers’ responsibilities included drilling and operating machinery, as well as blacksmithing and housekeeping.A climb of 700 stairs before work beganSouth Dakota’s state historian, Doane Robinson, proposed a large-scale sculpture in the Black Hills to attract visitors to the area. The concept was developed by sculptor Gutzon Borglum to turn it into a monument featuring four US presidents: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln.Reaching the worksite in itself was a demanding part of the job. The NPS records that the workers had to climb 700 steps to reach the top of the mountain to clock in for the day before beginning their duties. Notably, this was part of the routine while the project was operating, not an uninterrupted daily schedule across all 14 calendar years. The construction of the monument faced several interruptions, such as funding shortages and weather-related stoppages.The ones who were assigned to work on the steep granite face were usually lowered in bosun chairs attached to steel cables. These cables were approximately three-eighths of an inch thick. The federal agency describes the mountain’s face as roughly 500 feet high. Call boys helped coordinate this operation. They were positioned near the edge of the mountain and shouted messages between the workers in the suspended chairs and those operating the winches.How dynamite removed most of the mountainExplosives were central to the project due to the scale of the excavation. Around 90% of the carving was reportedly accomplished using dynamite. Powdermen prepared charges of specific sizes to remove calculated amounts of granite, instead of just blasting it indiscriminately. The workers were cleared from the mountain before a charge was detonated.Dynamite was used until only around three to six inches of rock remained beyond the intended carving surface. The process then shifted to a more precise method called honeycombing. Drillers made closely spaced holes in the rest of the granite. This weakened the granite, making it easy to remove the pieces by hand. Facers or bumper tools were then used by the workers to smooth the surfaces of the presidential faces.A dangerous project with lasting consequencesWhile there are no records of fatalities despite the hazardous conditions, the record should not be mistaken for an absence of serious occupational harm. Workers were exposed to fine granite dust. PBS’s American Experience reports that the lungs of several people who were associated with the project were permanently scarred by the dust.The project reached its final stage after Borglum died on March 6, 1941. His son, Lincoln Borglum, took up the responsibility for the remaining work. The final drilling took place on October 31 of that same year. The original plan depicted the presidents being sculpted down to their waists, but due to insufficient funding and practical constraints, the completed memorial consisted of four heads.You use AI every day. articles.title: After developing haircare products in Illinois, Annie Malone moved her small business to St. Louis in 1902; Poro products spread across the US, and she became one of the wealthiest Black women of her time
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring journey of Annie Turnbo Malone, a pioneering Black woman who founded Poro College and transformed the haircare industry with her innovative products, overcoming racial and gender barriers in the early 20th century.
articles.body: Achieving meaningful goals in the face of systemic barriers has always demanded relentless hard work and unwavering self-belief. Throughout history, while many were forced to yield to adversity, a determined few possessed the resilience to overcome every obstacle in their path. One such figure was Annie Turnbo Malone, who built a successful beauty business in an era shaped by racial and gender barriers.According to the accounts shared by the National Museum of African American History & Culture (NMAAHC), Annie was born in 1869 in Metropolis, Illinois, to formerly enslaved parents, both of whom died while she was young. From an early age, Annie recognized that for an African American woman, physical appearance and grooming were not just about personal fashion; they were expressions of identity, status, and resilience. She believed that improving scalp and hair health could make a meaningful difference in their livesDuring her childhood, Annie used to enjoy styling her sisters’ hair. This passion motivated her to build products that helped women embrace their natural beauty, rather than conform to the American standards of beauty that excluded them.As a Black woman entering the business world, Annie not only faced racial segregation but also gender discrimination. Despite these barriers, she stood her ground and began experimenting with chemistry to formulate safe, effective haircare solutions. She launched a line of products focused on improving scalp health and stimulating hair growth. This line featured various scalp preparations, including her flagship Wonderful Hair Grower.The history and rise of Poro CollegeAs cited in the historical records shared by the NMAAHC, after getting initial success in Illinois, Annie relocated to St. Louis, Missouri, in 1902 to expand her business. Over the next decade and a half, her business grew rapidly, leading her to establish Poro College Company (also known as Poro College) in 1918, a cosmetology center that was named after the Poro society, a secret organization in West Africa that embodied physicality and spirituality. Then, Poro College served not only as a training center, but also as a major engine of employment for African Americans, especially women.Annie’s Poro sales agents ranged in age from 16 to 80 and were trained to market her specialized products while applying the Poro system of scalp cleansing and hair conditioning. Throughout the company’s lifespan, tens of thousands of men and women sold Poro products across the United States and around the world.Beyond haircare items like the Wonderful Hair Grower, Special Hair Grower, and Tetter Relief, the company expanded into cosmetics, offering cold cream, lipstick, and even face powders in multiple shades of brown alongside white.Furthermore, Poro College offered African Americans, as well as major Black organizations like the National Negro Business League, a place to meet and discuss their ideas when the majority of public places excluded them.Poro Company faced severe setbacks In the 1920s, Annie’s Poro brand grew rapidly, increasing the value of her company and making her one of the wealthiest African American women. Even at the height of her fortune, she didn’t forget her roots and remembered to give back to her people. At that time, she contributed substantial funds to philanthropic initiatives in the St. Louis area and beyond, supporting institutions like Howard University.However, by the end of the decade, the Poro Company faced numerous financial setbacks driven by a bitter divorce settlement, costly legal disputes, and the economic and social devastation of the Great Depression. Despite the struggles, the company stayed afloat but at a fraction of its original scale.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A rare 1920 painting by Hilma af Klint passed through one family's hands after a 1995 purchase; estimated at 6 to 8 million Swedish kronor, it has sold for 128.9 million, a Nordic auction record
articles.summary: Art is often valued for the story it tells. When a family buys an art piece and keeps it at their house, it becomes more than an inanimate object.
articles.body: Art is often valued for the story it tells. When a family buys an art piece and keeps it at their house, it becomes more than an inanimate object. With each photograph taken in front of it, the conversations it listens to and the stories that unfold around it, the painting becomes more than just an object; it becomes a part of the family itself – an heirloom. During such situations, paintings become dual storytellers. They not only convey the story of the artist who created them and poured their soul into each brushstroke, but also that of the family that held them close. And when a painting decides to leave, it does not leave them empty-handed. articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to reach Delhi on Sunday for his first foreign bilateral trip - what's on agenda
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will begin a two-day state visit to India on Sunday, his first overseas bilateral state visit since taking
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will begin a two-day state visit to India on Sunday, his first overseas bilateral state visit since taking office in March."The visit will serve as an important opportunity to review our wide-ranging cooperative partnership with a forward-looking perspective, maximising mutual benefits for the peoples of both countries," Nepal's foreign ministry said in a statement.Shah, an ex-Kathmandu mayor and a former rapper, will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation comprising finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign affairs minister Shishir Khanal, his chief advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior government officials.Balendra Shah's itinerary in New DelhiShah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, after which they will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects. The two sides will also sign and exchange bilateral agreements covering various areas of cooperation.The two prime ministers will address a joint press conference, followed by a luncheon hosted by PM Modi in honour of the visiting Nepali leader.During his visit, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tributes at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which aims to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two countries.What's likely to be discussedAccording to ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, India and Nepal are expected to discuss issues including development cooperation and people-to-people ties."All these issues will be discussed: development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy ties, connectivity, and some of the newer areas of cooperation such as startups, technology, innovation, and sports. Cricket links have also become an important connection between India and Nepal. This is a very important visit for us," Jaiswal told reporters at a weekly news briefing in New Delhi on Friday.Shah is also expected to discuss Indian assistance for the reconstruction of areas affected by the devastating floods in August, Reuters reported, citing Nepalese officials.The August 26 floods killed 1,500 people, left more than 5,200 missing and destroyed roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes.Nepal is also likely to discuss with India an additional route for commercial flights from the west to Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, the birthplace of Gautam Buddha, and the tourist city of Pokhara.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: No answers, no funding: US lawmaker turns up heat on Musk over Ukraine Starshield disruptions
articles.summary: A satellite network that has become a lifeline for Ukraine's war effort is now threatening to become a major headache for Elon Musk.
articles.body: A satellite network that has become a lifeline for Ukraine's war effort is now threatening to become a major headache for Elon Musk.A senior US lawmaker has threatened to block funding for SpaceX's government projects unless the company explains who ordered restrictions on Ukraine's access to its military satellite communications system, Starshield.US Representative Jim Himes, who is set to become chairman of the House Intelligence Committee in January 2027, has warned that Congress could withhold funding for SpaceX-developed government systems if the company fails to explain the restrictions.In a letter to director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, Himes said, "Simply, our committee cannot authorize funds for the development of government systems that the government will not fully control", CNN reported.He has also sought a meeting with SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, demanding an explanation of the restrictions imposed on Ukraine's Starshield service in October, including who authorised them and whether the company acted independently or followed instructions from a US government official.Himes has warned that SpaceX's potential unilateral modification of a government contract, along with its failure to respond adequately to congressional oversight, raises concerns about the company's other government contracts.He has indicated that lawmakers could use their funding powers to restrict money for specific SpaceX projects until the company provides satisfactory answers.The warning comes amid growing concerns over disruptions to SpaceX's satellite communications services in Ukraine, where Starlink and Starshield have become important to the country's military operations.The controversy stems from repeated disruptions to SpaceX's satellite communications services in Ukraine, where Starlink and Starshield have become critical to military operations.While Starlink is SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, Starshield is its military-grade system developed for government and national security requirements.Between October 13 and October 24, restrictions on satellite connectivity disrupted Ukrainian military operations, including the use of interceptor drones deployed to defend cities against Russian attacks. The limitations reportedly affected connectivity for fast-moving drones, raising concerns over Ukraine's ability to counter Russian aerial threats.The issue resurfaced on November 12, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his military had reported significant Starshield disruptions along the entire front line and in Russian-occupied territories.He said the interruptions appeared to be systematic rather than random technical failures and that Kyiv was seeking clarification from Washington. The renewed disruption triggered concerns over Ukraine's battlefield communications and its ability to defend against Russian drone attacks, particularly as Moscow intensified strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure.The controversy also triggered conflicting explanations from Washington and SpaceX over who ordered the restrictions.Musk maintained that Starshield was controlled by the US government and that decisions on its use rested with the American military.US President Donald Trump denied ordering the restrictions and said he did not know who was responsible.Secretary of state Marco Rubio, meanwhile, indicated that decisions regarding Starlink access rested with SpaceX, while a Pentagon official told CNN that defence secretary Pete Hegseth had no prior knowledge or involvement.The conflicting accounts have raised questions over who exercises authority over a military communications system operated by a private company.You use AI every day. articles.body: In her first public discussion of her cancer experience, Catherine, the Princess of Wales, has reflected on how the disease "does change you"."It changes your body, it changes you physically... healing is a journey," she says in the trailer for "Heal," a documentary exploring life beyond her diagnosis of an unspecified form of cancer, which was made public in March 2024."But there's a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you... Often it is through pain that we realise that there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that," the future Queen of England, who is now in remission, says."Heal" will premiere on BBC in the UK next Sunday before airing internationally through NBCUniversal in the US, Channel 9 in Australia, and CTV and Noovo in Canada over the following weeks."As she (Catherine) undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the film follows the Princess on a personal journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes," Kensington Palace said in a statement."Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal," it added.The palace also noted that through the documentary, Catherine hopes to help others "navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis."All proceeds from the documentary's international distribution will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity in London.Catherine, formerly known as Kate Middleton, is married to Prince William, the elder son of King Charles III and heir to the British throne. articles.title: A Brooklyn man bought a house in 1985 and added his wife to the deed three years later, but was removed from the US in 1999; after their 2007 divorce, a court upheld his right to seek a sale of the shared home
articles.summary: A Brooklyn man who bought a house in 1985 and added his wife to its ownership papers three years later has won the right to seek its sale, more than two
articles.body: A Brooklyn man who bought a house in 1985 and added his wife to its ownership papers three years later has won the right to seek its sale, more than two decades after he was removed from the United States. A New York appeals court has ruled that his former wife cannot prevent him from pursuing the property claim simply because their divorce was finalised without addressing ownership of the house.According to Law Justia, the ruling was delivered on November 18, 2026, by the Appellate Division of the New York Supreme Court, Second Department, in the case of Nelson v Nelson. According to the court's decision, Clyde Nelson and Verna Nelson married in 1977. They purchased the Brooklyn property in 1985, with the title initially held only in Clyde's name. In 1988, the ownership documents were changed to include both spouses.Verna had been in sole possession of the property since around 1995. The court record says this continued after Clyde was removed from the United States in 1999. He has not returned since. The couple's marriage formally ended in 2007, when a divorce judgment was entered after Clyde failed to appear in the proceedings. However, the judgment did not settle the ownership or division of their Brooklyn property.Why did the dispute return to court years after the divorce?In 2019, Clyde filed a lawsuit seeking partition and sale of the property. A partition action is a legal process through which a co-owner can ask a court to divide jointly owned property or order its sale when the owners cannot agree on what should happen to it.Verna asked the court to dismiss his complaint. She argued that Clyde should have raised his ownership claim during their divorce proceedings and that he was therefore barred from pursuing it later.Her argument relied on two legal principles: ‘res judicata,’ which generally prevents parties from bringing claims that have already been decided, and ‘collateral estoppel,’ which prevents them from relitigating issues that were previously determined. However, the court found that the divorce judgment had not actually decided what should happen to the property.According to the judgment, Verna's divorce complaint had stated that the couple had "divided up the marital property, and no claim will be made by either party under equitable distribution." The divorce judgment did not include any order disposing of the Brooklyn house.The appeals court explained that the divorce had converted their ownership from a tenancy by the entirety to a tenancy in common. In simple terms, both former spouses continued to hold ownership interests in the property, even after their marriage ended.It concluded that the divorce judgment had not extinguished Clyde's ownership rights or prevented him from seeking a sale.Appeals court upholds his right to pursue the saleThe case had earlier been considered by the Supreme Court in Kings County. In an order dated September 15, 2022, the lower court rejected Verna's request to dismiss the lawsuit and ruled that Clyde's right to seek partition had been established. It also referred the matter to a special referee for further proceedings. Verna appealed that decision.On November 18, 2026, the Second Department affirmed the lower court's order, with costs. The court held that Clyde was not barred by res judicata or collateral estoppel from asserting his ownership interest, including through a request for partition.The ruling does not mean the house has already been sold or that the court has determined how much money either former spouse will receive. It confirms that Clyde can continue with his legal effort to seek partition and sale of the jointly owned property.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ladakh records 70% voting in panchayat polls, 52% in municpal elections
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Ladakh Saturday recorded 70.03% turnout in panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal council polls, held for the first time since it was
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Ladakh Saturday recorded 70.03% turnout in panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal council polls, held for the first time since it was declared a Union Territory in 2019.The young and the elderly, women and men, first-time voters, monks and people from every walk of life exercised their democratic right across villages and towns. The state election commission said the enthusiastic participation reflected the people’s deep commitment to grassroots democracy and local self-governance.The local body polls were held amid protests led by Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) seeking deferment of Dec 4 elections to eight autonomous hill development councils, citing the harsh winter.The panchayat elections covered 192 Panchayat Halqas across eight districts, comprising 192 sarpanch positions and 1,428 panch seats. Of these, 55 sarpanches and 1,186 panches were elected unopposed, while polling was conducted for the remaining 137 sarpanch and 242 panch seats.The municipal council elections covered 38 wards, comprising 21 in Leh and 17 in Kargil. Polling was conducted in all 21 wards of Leh, while four wards in Kargil were filled unopposed and polling was held in the remaining 13 wards.Election authorities had made elaborate arrangements for the smooth conduct of polling. In Zanskar, helicopters were deployed to airlift polling teams to three remote and road-inaccessible polling stations, enabling the conduct of elections in some of the most isolated settlements.Ladakh lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena described the day as historic for the region, saying the overwhelming participation in the polls “is a powerful testament to people’s unshakeable faith in the democratic process and local self-governance”.However, LAB co-chairperson Chering Dorjay Lakrook and member Sonam Wangchuk alleged at a joint press conference in Leh that a “large number of people” had been left out of the electoral rolls. “I wanted to go to my own village to vote but I was told that the polling booth there had been shifted to another village. That is why villagers in my village boycotted the polls,” Wangchuk said.Wangchuk, who stepped out of his house Saturday after the administration withdrew the security cordon around it, accused the administration of “behaving like a rogue state” and alleged that elections were being imposed on the people of Ladakh.The administration’s alleged “anti-Ladakh measures” were fuelling anger among the people, he said, warning that the growing resentment would have serious implications for national security.The strategically important region “should not be left at the mercy of administrators who behave like a bull in a china shop”, the climate activist said, urging the prime minister and the defence minister to intervene and ensure that the people of Ladakh got their due.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Beverly Hills penthouse listed for $27.5 million has sold for $21 million after only 10 days on the market; the nearly 4,700-square-foot home has a private rooftop pool and monthly building dues of $18,740
articles.summary: A luxury penthouse in Beverly Hills has sold for $21 million after spending just 10 days on the market.
articles.body: A luxury penthouse in Beverly Hills has sold for $21 million after spending just 10 days on the market. The sale set a local record as the most expensive condominium deal in the city in 2026. The three-bedroom home, known as Penthouse C at the Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills, was first listed for $27.5 million before selling for about 24 per cent less on 17 November. According to Realtor.com and The Real Deal, an international buyer whose identity has not been revealed purchased the property at 9900 South Santa Monica Boulevard. Although the final sale price was $6.5 million below the original asking price, the deal was still the fourth most expensive condominium sale in Los Angeles County in 2026, based on Zillow property records reviewed by The Real Deal.Inside the 4,699-square-foot residenceMultiple Listing Service records show that Penthouse C has 4,699 square feet of indoor living space, five bathrooms, and a private garage with room for four cars. At the final price of $21 million, the property sold for about $4,469 per square foot. Its original asking price worked out to around $5,852 per square foot. New York-based interior and furniture designer Samuel Amoia designed the home. Its features include a custom floating staircase with a skylight, a two-sided fireplace made from carved stone, and large sliding glass doors that open onto spacious terraces.The upper floor leads to a private rooftop deck measuring 2,169 square feet. It has a 25-foot swimming pool, a spa, and an outdoor kitchen. The main bedroom suite includes two walk-in wardrobes, a dressing room with a window, and a bathroom designed to feel like a luxury spa. There is also a separate California room with a wet bar, offering more space for entertaining guests. According to Resident Magazine, the model home was decorated with collectible furniture and artwork. These included a dining chandelier by Blue Green Works, a glass seed table by Max Zinser, a stool by Brett Robinson, and a bronze mirror by Gergei Erdei."With only 17 residences in a highly serviced building, there's a sense of intimacy and individuality that makes the penthouses at Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills feel truly private. The design needed to reflect that sensibility," Amoia told Galerie Magazine when the penthouse was listed.High monthly fees and hotel-style servicesOwning the penthouse also comes with high monthly costs. Listing records cited by Realtor.com and The Real Deal show that the homeowner association (HOA) fees for the property are $18,740 per month. This adds up to nearly $225,000 a year. These fees pay for staff available around the clock and hotel-style services managed by Rosewood Hotels & Resorts. Services include a dedicated director of residences, a full-time concierge, and a personal residential butler. Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills was completed in 2024 by developers Nahla Capital and GPI Companies. The building stands on the former site of the historic Friars Club. It is Rosewood's first standalone residential project in California without an attached hotel. Designed by Danish architect Thomas Juul-Hansen, the four-storey building has just 17 homes above an underground garage with 148 parking spaces. It also includes 12,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. According to Galerie Magazine, hospitality group Noble 33 plans to open two Japanese restaurants in the ground-floor commercial area in 2027. The venues will include a steakhouse and an izakaya, a Japanese restaurant that serves small dishes and drinks.How the Beverly Hills location helped the buyer save on taxesThe sale was handled by Tomer Fridman and Amir Ensani of The Beverly Hills Estates, along with Sally Forster Jones of Compass. Speaking to The Real Deal, Ensani said the overseas buyer was specifically searching for a home with hotel-style services and a well-known hospitality brand. The buyer also wanted to avoid the City of Los Angeles transfer tax, commonly called Measure ULA or the "mansion tax". Measure ULA charges a 4 per cent transfer tax on property sales above $5 million and a 5.5 per cent tax on sales exceeding $10 million within the City of Los Angeles. However, Beverly Hills is an independent city outside Los Angeles city limits. This means properties there are not subject to the additional tax. By purchasing the $21 million penthouse in Beverly Hills instead of a property across the city boundary in neighbouring Los Angeles, the buyer saved more than $1.15 million in city transfer taxes. The sale adds to continued buyer interest in the 17-home development.
