articles.title: A Texas businessman who prosecutors say never served in the military allegedly posed as a veteran and federal contracting officer to win more than $1.6 million in government contracts and supply counterfeit equipment
articles.summary: A 24-year-old Texas man is facing federal fraud charges after allegedly creating a false military background, impersonating government officials and
articles.body: A 24-year-old Texas man is facing federal fraud charges after allegedly creating a false military background, impersonating government officials and supplying counterfeit equipment to the US Army. According to the US Department of Justice, the San Antonio resident secured at least 70 federal contracts worth more than $1.6 million in obligated funds through the alleged scheme. The case has also been reported by the San Antonio Express-News, Stars and Stripes and Task & Purpose. The accused, Marcelo Fascino, established a company called PGCE LLC in La Vernia, Texas, in May 2022 to pursue government contracts. Prosecutors allege that he falsely presented the business as veteran-owned, service-disabled veteran-owned and women-owned, despite having no military service himself. These classifications would have made the company eligible to compete for contracts reserved for businesses meeting specific ownership requirements.However, the alleged misrepresentation extended beyond the company’s credentials. Investigators say Fascino also posed as a federal contracting officer, claiming to represent several government departments and military agencies to gain an advantage over competing suppliers.According to the indictment, he allegedly created fake email signatures and modified official contracting documents, replacing the names and contact details of legitimate government officers with his own. When approaching suppliers for price quotations on Army and National Guard contracts, he allegedly identified himself as Staff Sergeant Marcelo Fascino, despite never having served in the military.Prosecutors believe the impersonation was intended to restrict competition. Suppliers who thought they were already communicating with an authorised government contracting officer could mistakenly assume they had submitted their bids, potentially missing the actual deadlines for competing contracts.The agencies he allegedly claimed to represent included the US Army, National Guard, Marine Corps, Air Force, Coast Guard, Army Corps of Engineers and Department of the Interior. The investigation also uncovered allegations involving the supply of counterfeit and non-compliant military equipment. Court documents state that Fascino allegedly provided ammunition, weapon lights and optical equipment that did not match the specifications or quality of the products he had agreed to deliver.In one instance, he allegedly supplied the Army with Chinese-made weapon lights while claiming they had been manufactured in the United States. Prosecutors also allege that he fabricated a letter bearing the name of a rifle optics manufacturer in an attempt to persuade Army contracting personnel to accept counterfeit Chinese-made optics instead of the genuine products originally promised.The substituted equipment was allegedly significantly cheaper than the products specified in the contracts, according to federal investigators. Between October 2022 and May 2024, PGCE LLC was awarded at least 70 federal contracts, involving more than $1.6 million in obligated government funds, the indictment states. The case has raised concerns about the alleged misuse of programmes intended to provide contracting opportunities to veteran-owned and other qualifying small businesses.Fascino was indicted by a federal grand jury in San Antonio on November 4, 2026. The charges were publicly announced by US Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas on November 17. He faces three counts of wire fraud and three counts of false personation of a federal officer or employee. If convicted, each wire fraud count carries a maximum sentence of 30 years in federal prison, while each false personation charge carries a maximum of three years. Any eventual sentence would be determined by a federal judge.The investigation involves the Department of War Office of Inspector General, General Services Administration Office of Inspector General, Army Criminal Investigation Division and Department of the Interior Office of Inspector General. Assistant US Attorney Eric Yuen and Special Assistant US Attorney Jay Porier are handling the prosecution.The case remains pending, and the charges against Fascino are allegations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Reflecting on Purana Qila's history, Pakistan minister invokes Humanyun & Sher Shah Suri at SCO civilisational dialogue to assert cultural diversity
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Venue of the first civilisational dialogue under the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Forum, Purana Qila symbolised civilisational continuity
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Venue of the first civilisational dialogue under the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Forum, Purana Qila symbolised civilisational continuity but in the case of Pakistan with a different perspective. In marked contrast to India, which It’s minister Musadik Masood Malik on Saturday chose to emphasise that the foundations of the Old Fort were laid by Humanyun whose origins lay in central Asia and that its construction was carried forward by Sher Shah Suri who came from Afghanistan as he sought to focus on the sub continent’s cultural diversity.“Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions,” Malik said.India has touted Old Fort as the perfect venue for the meet with its multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic ‘Mahabharata’. As part of the retelling of the approximately 3000-year long history of the site, India showcased nine layers of continuity--among them the standing ramparts built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, around 1533 CE.Reflecting on the excavations at the site, Malik said, “Delhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown stronger”.During his inaugural speech on Friday Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also reflected on the history of Purana Qila to assert India’s civilisational journey going back thousands of years to the Mahabharata period. He also visited the ‘Mahabharata Pavillion - Anant: A rare 18th century Mahabharata scroll’ and the exhibition ‘Astitva’ offering an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence, that have been curated for the leaders from SCO countries to see.Day two of the Fourm saw ministers of all participating nations make statements. Malik who happens to be the Climate Change and Environmental Coordination referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: UK should only rejoin EU if it innovates on technology, Blair warns
articles.summary: The former prime minister argues the European Union is probably moving in the wrong direction on technology innovation.
articles.body:
Former prime minister Sir Tony Blair has said Britain should only rejoin the European Union if it reforms - and allows more innovation on technology.

Speaking to The Sunday Times , Sir Tony said: "I was painted as saying Britain should just go back and rejoin - I'm not saying that - it's heavily conditioned."

Sir Tony was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, and told the paper: "I do think Brexit was a real mistake."

But he added the debate was different now than it was in 2016.

Referencing the need for technology innovation, he said Europe could and "probably are" moving in the wrong direction.

He said: "The problem if we go back and join Europe is that; I can't say that the technology revolution is the single biggest thing, and then if Europe moves in the wrong direction on technology innovation, which they might do and presently probably are doing, that it's a good idea for Britain to rejoin. That's what's changed in this last ten years."

He argued Britain should have an ambition to reform the EU.

But he added that we have to be "prepared to walk away from that negotiation" and need to make our own economy and tech sector strong.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham this week agreed what he called a "win-win" deal with the EU.

The agreement covered British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also announced that the trading bloc and the UK are launching a digital partnership, including areas like artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum technology.

The EU and Britain "have enormous potential to innovate together", she added.

On artificial intelligence, Sir Tony said that "AI is like fire - it can cook your food and burn your house down".

Sir Tony added the risks of AI are "very considerable" and that tech "can be used for good or bad". "It's a new world," he said.

But he fears the UK does not have the same "dynamism" and "energy" as other countries when it comes to the fast-changing technology sector.

Burnham was in Brussels on Friday to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU - which originally began under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

European Council President António Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK.

The prime minister added that beyond the deal "we do need to consider what is the right long-term relationship".

He said over the coming months before the next UK-EU summit both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at what those options are.

He fell short of discussing whether the UK could rejoin the EU.

Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says

Burnham gets his first taste of EU dealmaking and seems hungry for more

What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the UK-EU deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people".

Earlier this year, Sir Tony urged PM Andy Burnham to restart negotiations on the possibility of the UK rejoining the EU - but with caveats.

Writing in a paper from the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change published in September, the former prime minister wrote: "We should be clear that we want back into a formal relationship with the EU. But it must be a Europe on a credible path to reform."

"This is not about rerunning the debates of 2016 but taking a new approach rooted in the reality of 2026," he added.

articles.title: IShowSpeed teases huge announcement after completing GTA 6 following 52-hour livestream
articles.summary: IShowSpeed has completed the story mode of GTA 6 after spending 52 hours playing the game without sleeping.
articles.body: IShowSpeed has completed the story mode of GTA 6 after spending 52 hours playing the game without sleeping. The popular streamer surprised fans by continuing his livestream for more than two days, even though he had earlier promised not to rush through the game. After finally reaching the ending, Speed became emotional and broke down in tears. However, there was another surprise before he ended the stream. The streamer teased a huge announcement, leaving fans curious about what he plans to reveal next.IShowSpeed hints at a huge announcement after finishing GTA 6After completing the GTA 6 story, IShowSpeed told his viewers that he had a huge announcement coming soon. However, he did not share any details about what the announcement could be.This has left fans wondering what the streamer is preparing next. He also did not give a date for the announcement, so viewers will have to wait for more information.Before signing off, Speed spoke about his experience playing Rockstar Games' latest title. He said that he had spent 52 hours playing the game and had not slept once during the livestream."Bro, I just played this game for 52 hours," he told his viewers after watching the ending. He also appeared shocked by what he had just experienced.Speed had earlier said that he did not want to rush through GTA 6 because he wanted his fans to enjoy playing the game themselves. However, his excitement kept him playing much longer than planned.GTA 6 livestream goes from planned 12 hours to a 52-hour marathonBefore GTA 6 launched, IShowSpeed told his fans that he would stream the game for around 12 hours. He also said that he wanted to take his time instead of rushing through the story.However, things changed once he started playing. Speed went live on YouTube and Twitch at 9 PM ET on November 18 and continued playing for more than two days.Around 40 hours into the stream, he had completed about 82% of the main story. He believed he needed around 12 more hours to finish the game.His marathon also faced a major problem when his PS5 crashed during a cutscene. Speed feared that he had lost his progress because he was not sure whether the game had been saved. Thankfully, the autosave feature worked, and he returned to the game with 88% progress.After the long wait, Speed finally completed the story and watched the credits roll.IShowSpeed's 52 hour GTA 6 livestream became a whole lot more than he'd originally intended. A PS5 crash midway through, an emotional reaction at the end, and fans who stayed until the very last moment to watch it all unfold.
